participants.name: Predator Free Dunedin
participants.summary: Umbrella trust/partnership of more than 20 established Dunedin volunteer groups and larger organisations delivering landscape-scale predator control across Dunedin; delivers three flagship projects (Possum Free Peninsula, City Sanctuary, The Halo Project).
participants.detail: Regional coordination hub; holds relationships with nearly every Dunedin-area predator control group and with councils, DOC and PF2050.

participants.name: Possum Free Peninsula
participants.summary: Project to remove possums from the Otago Peninsula, delivered on the ground by Otago Peninsula Biodiversity Group under the Predator Free Dunedin umbrella.
participants.detail: Operational possum eradication footprint covering the whole Peninsula.

participants.name: City Sanctuary
participants.summary: Urban predator-control project covering Dunedin city, linking backyard and reserve trapping to the large-scale control on the Peninsula and north of the city; runs a public Trap.NZ project.
participants.detail: Urban trapping network and volunteer coordination across Dunedin city suburbs.

participants.name: City Sanctuary Trap.NZ project
participants.summary: Public Trap.NZ project used to register and record backyard and reserve traps across Dunedin City.
participants.detail: Live trap-record platform; useful for mapping actual trap coverage.

participants.name: The Halo Project
participants.localityRaw: Dunedin northern halo; Waikouaiti; Karitāne; Blueskin Bay
participants.summary: Community-led predator control and habitat restoration in the 'halo' of land surrounding Orokonui Ecosanctuary, plus the Beyond Orokonui and Source to Sea programmes.
participants.detail: Large rural/peri-urban trapping network with paid field leads and rangers; key partner in Predator Free Dunedin.

participants.name: Landscape Connections Trust
participants.summary: Charitable trust that governs the Halo Project, Beyond Orokonui and Source to Sea; ORC ECO Fund and Otago Community Trust grant recipient for the Mihiwaka - Kāpuka-Taumāhaka/Mt Cargill project.
participants.detail: Governance body holding funding contracts and employing field staff across the Dunedin northern halo.

participants.name: Source to Sea
participants.summary: Catchment-to-coast restoration and predator control programme run by Landscape Connections Trust in the Waikouaiti/Karitāne area.
participants.detail: Employs rangers doing on-ground trapping and riparian restoration work.

participants.name: Beyond Orokonui
participants.summary: Project extending predator control beyond the Orokonui Ecosanctuary fence into surrounding private and public land.
participants.detail: Buffer-zone control protecting the fenced sanctuary.

participants.name: Orokonui Ecosanctuary
participants.summary: 307-hectare predator-fenced coastal forest ecosanctuary north of Dunedin, run by the Otago Natural History Trust; anchor site for the Halo Project and Predator Free Dunedin.

participants.name: Otago Natural History Trust
